Addition Polymers: A polymer is a very large molecule made of many repeating units (monomers). In addition polymerization, monomers with a C=C double bond join without losing any atoms. Ethene forms poly(ethene) (polyethylene), propene forms poly(propene), chloroethene forms PVC, tetrafluoroethene forms PTFE (Teflon) and styrene forms polystyrene. The repeating unit is written with the double bond opened: -(CH2-CH2)n-. Properties depend on the structure: low-density poly(ethene) has branched chains and is flexible, high-density has linear chains and is stronger. Thermoplastics soften on heating and can be reshaped, while thermosetting plastics have cross-links and do not soften. Most addition polymers are not biodegradable, so recycling and disposal are environmental issues.
Condensation Polymers: In condensation polymerization, monomers with two functional groups join and a small molecule, usually water, is released at each link. Polyesters (such as PET) form from a dicarboxylic acid and a diol through ester links: n HOOC-R-COOH + n HO-R'-OH -> polyester + 2n H2O. Polyamides (nylon) form from a dicarboxylic acid and a diamine through amide (peptide) links; nylon-6,6 uses hexanedioic acid and 1,6-diaminohexane. Condensation polymers can be broken down by hydrolysis, so they can be more easily degraded or recycled than addition polymers. Natural polymers such as proteins (polyamides), starch and cellulose (polysaccharides) and DNA are also formed by condensation. Kevlar is an aromatic polyamide with very high strength.
Carbohydrates and Lipids: Carbohydrates have the general formula Cx(H2O)y. Monosaccharides (glucose, fructose, C6H12O6) are the simplest sugars; two join by a glycosidic link with loss of water to give a disaccharide (sucrose = glucose + fructose; maltose, lactose). Polysaccharides such as starch (energy storage in plants), glycogen (in animals) and cellulose (plant cell walls) are polymers of glucose. Hydrolysis with acid or enzymes breaks them into monosaccharides. Lipids (fats and oils) are triesters of glycerol (propane-1,2,3-triol) and three fatty acids. Saturated fatty acids have no C=C and give solid fats, unsaturated ones have C=C and give liquid oils. Hydrogenation of oils makes margarine, and the hydrolysis of fat with NaOH gives soap (saponification). Lipids store more energy per gram (about 38 kJ/g) than carbohydrates (about 17 kJ/g).
Proteins and Amino Acids: Amino acids have the general structure H2N-CH(R)-COOH: an amino group, a carboxyl group and a side chain R on the central carbon. In solution they exist as zwitterions (H3N+-CH(R)-COO-) and can act as acids and bases, so they buffer. Twenty amino acids form proteins; two join by a peptide (amide) bond with loss of water, forming dipeptides and long polypeptide chains. Protein structure has four levels: primary (amino acid sequence), secondary (alpha helix and beta sheet held by hydrogen bonds), tertiary (3D folding stabilized by disulfide bridges, ionic bonds, hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions) and quaternary (several chains together). Enzymes are protein catalysts with an active site that fits a specific substrate (lock-and-key / induced fit). Heat and extreme pH denature proteins. Hydrolysis with acid gives the amino acids.
Nucleic Acids and Metabolism: Nucleic acids (DNA and RNA) are polymers of nucleotides. A nucleotide has a sugar (deoxyribose in DNA, ribose in RNA), a phosphate group and a base. DNA bases are adenine (A), thymine (T), guanine (G) and cytosine (C); in RNA thymine is replaced by uracil (U). DNA is a double helix with the strands held by hydrogen bonds between base pairs: A pairs with T (two hydrogen bonds) and G pairs with C (three). The sequence of bases is the genetic code: three bases (a codon) code for one amino acid. DNA replicates semi-conservatively; RNA is made from DNA (transcription) and used to make proteins (translation). Metabolism includes catabolism (breaking down molecules and releasing energy) and anabolism (building molecules using energy). ATP is the energy currency of the cell: ATP + H2O -> ADP + phosphate, delta G is about -30 kJ/mol. Photosynthesis: 6 CO2 + 6 H2O -> C6H12O6 + 6 O2; respiration is the reverse.
